title: Remember what you have seen
summary: Sets and maps answer "have I seen this before?" instantly, turning slow nested loops into one pass.

sections.heading: The slow way and the fast way
body: Comparing every item with every other item needs a loop inside a loop. With 1,000 items that is about a million comparisons.
Instead, walk the list once and remember what you have passed. Checking a set or map takes about the same time however big it is.

sections.heading: Sets: have I seen this?
body: A set holds each value at most once and answers "is this in here?" quickly.

sections.heading: Maps: where did I see it?
body: A map (a dict in Python) remembers something about each value, such as the index where you first met it.

mistakes: In JavaScript, `x in array` checks indexes, not values. Use `array.includes(x)` or a `Set`.
Checking `x in some_list` inside a loop in Python is slow on big lists. Make it a set first.
Plain JavaScript objects turn keys into strings; a `Map` keeps `1` and `'1'` apart.
